title: Aswan
standfirst: Aswan is the southern end of most Nile cruises: granite islands, feluccas, Nubian villages and the temple of Philae. It is one of the stops in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: What to see
paragraphs: Philae, the temple of Isis, moved to a nearby island when the dams were built and reached by motorboat. The High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk in the old granite quarries. A felucca sail around Elephantine and Kitchener’s Island.

sections.heading: Beyond Aswan
paragraphs: Abu Simbel is the great excursion from Aswan, by road or by air. Nubian villages on the West Bank can be visited by boat.

sections.heading: Time in Aswan
paragraphs: Cruises usually spend a day in Aswan. It is a good place to add a night, for Abu Simbel or simply for the river.

faqs.q: Can I visit Abu Simbel from a cruise?
faqs.a: Yes, as an optional excursion from Aswan, usually leaving very early in the morning.
Often, on cruises that end or start in Aswan. Each cruise lists what is included.
